newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks expected soft, focus on rates.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks expected soft, focus on rates.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to trade softer on Monday, with investors focused on the interest rate outlook and awaiting U.S. economic data with some caution, analysts said.
"Right now investor focus will be back on interest rates. Today the market might test 12,600," said Ricky Tam, research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hang Seng Index rose 104.58 points last week to close at 12,645.76 on Friday.
"The market might test 12,550 this week because there is a lot of important economic data," said Tam.
The U.S. first quarter employment cost index is due on Tuesday and April employment data on Friday.
"We have some concerns about all this strong data coming out and pushing the (bond) yield up," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
"I think the market is going to be lacklustre. Wall Street was off a bit. We have seen a sharp rise in red chips so people are a bit cautious," he said.
Tam said the expiry of April Hang Seng Index futures on Tuesday could also prompt some caution on Monday.
